This variable contains the National Primary Drinking Water Regulations (NPDWR) standards, which include maximum contaminant level (MCL) and treatment techniques (TT) action levels. These are legally enforceable primary standards and treatment techniques that apply to public water systems. https://www.epa.gov/ground-water-and-drinking-water/national-primary-drinking-water-regulations#Inorganic

This variable contains the National Secondary Drinking Water Regulations (NSDWRs) standards, which are non-mandatory water quality standards. The EPA does not enforce these "secondary maximum contaminant levels" (SMCLs). They are established as guidelines to assist public water systems in managing their drinking water for aesthetic considerations, such as taste, color, and odor. These contaminants are not considered to present a risk to human health at the SMCL.https://www.epa.gov/sdwa/secondary-drinking-water-standards-guidance-nuisance-chemicals

This variable contains the Action Level standard for Lead and Copper, based on the Lead and Copper rule of 199. https://www.epa.gov/dwreginfo/lead-and-copper-rule. The treatment technique for the rule requires systems to monitor drinking water at customer taps. If lead concentrations exceed an action level of 15 ppb or copper concentrations exceed an action level of 1.3 ppm in more than 10% of customer taps sampled, the system must undertake a number of additional actions to control corrosion.

This variable contains the North Carolina groundwater (NC GW) standards, which are the maximum allowable concentrations of contaminants in groundwater in NC. Regulations pertaining to the classifications and water quality standards applicable to groundwaters of North Carolina are located in Title 15A of the North Carolina Administrative Code, Subchapter 2L, Sections .0100, .0200, .0300 and .0400. https://files.nc.gov/ncdeq/documents/files/02L%20Groundwater%20Standards%20Table%205-21%202013_0.pdf

This variable contains the North Carolina Interim Maximum Allowable Concentration (NC IMAC) standards. Any person may petition the NC Division of Water Resources Director to establish an IMAC for a substance for which a NC GW standard has not been established.

This variable contains the screening limits that were established in the Coal Ash Management Act (CAMA)  of 2014. As part of this act, private drinking water wells within 1,500 feet of designated facilities were evaluated for numerous constituents that could indicate the presence of any contamination associated with coal ash. The standards ilsted in this variable are the health-protective performance standards set to evaulte water filtration systems installed in eligible homes. The values included in this table were the levels reported on the well water test report sent to eligible well owners. https://www.ncleg.net/Sessions/2013/Bills/Senate/PDF/S729v6.pdf

This variable details if the EPA MCL is a special type of MCL. Specifically, if it is derived from the Radionuclides rule or a is a TT action level. The Treatment Technique (TT) action level is the point at which a public water systems must take specific actions to mitigate exposure and reduce levels of either Copper or Lead. This was established in the Lead and Copper rule of 1991. https://www.epa.gov/dwreginfo/lead-and-copper-rule. The Radionuclides Rule set new monitoring provisions for community water systems. It sets enforcable MCLs for radionuclides. This rule went into effect in 2000. https://www.epa.gov/dwreginfo/radionuclides-rule
